title: Dashboard heuristics field notes - Jan 2026
content:
Purpose
These are my field notes from working through the last two oncall rotations and the rollout prep for Q1 model changes. Goal: capture lightweight heuristics that help build small, investigative dashboards (microdash) and keep metric definitions consistent across panels. This is intentionally informal — stash of ideas + checklist for quick experiments.

Quick wins (things we can do in a 1/2 day)
- Add a KV-warmth percentile sparkline to the model instance table (p50/p90/p99 of prefix-hit-rate)
- Expose a single-pane view: requests-per-second, median token-latency, 95th token-latency, error-rate, and a small table of top-5 tenants by cost increase (last 1h)
- Add trace link column in the request table (shortened trace id clickable) so operators can jump straight to session reconstruction

Signal sanity checklist (metric def + why it matters + quick collection note)
- request.count: total inference requests received. Collect as counter, tag by route/model/region. Use ppm (per minute) for real-time dashboards.
- token.latency.ms: per-token generation latency (ms). Histogram + p50/p90/p95/p99. IMPORTANT: compute as server-side delta between token start and token end spans to avoid client skew.
- request.end-to-end.ms: from ingress to final token emitted for non-streaming requests. For streaming, use first-byte latency separately.
- kv.prefix-hit-rate: fraction of requests where prefix KV cache satisfied at least one KV hit. Derive from per-request attributes; rollup as p50/p90/p99 across instances.
- model.queue-time.ms: time spent waiting on an execution queue (when batching enabled). Critical for identifying underprovisioning.
- error.rate: count of responses with 5xx or internal-check failures divided by request.count. Tag by failure_type attribute (OOM, timeout, model-mismatch, infra).
- tenant.cost.delta: incremental cost per tenant (estimate from tokens * cost-per-token config). Useful as a guardrail during rollouts.

Trace annotation conventions (short conventions to standardize spans)
- Root span name: inference.request (attrs: request.id, tenant.id, route, model.version, region)
- Spawned spans:
  - auth.check (attrs: identity.source)
  - routing.lookup (attrs: route.policy, fallback=true|false)
  - batch.wait (attrs: batch.size, batch.timeout_ms)
  - exec.kernel (attrs: model, device, quantized=true|false, kernel.name)
  - kv.lookup (attrs: kv.key_count, kv.hits, kv.policy)
  - token.emit (attrs: token.index, token.source=kv|exec|prefix)
- For every exec.kernel span include: memory.peak_mb and gpu.util_pct. For long-lived requests mark trace-level tag slow=true if p95 token latency > 500ms.
- Use attribute trace.phase for quick filtering values: ingress|routing|batching|exec|emit|egress

Dashboard templates (microdash wireframes)
1) Microtriage (single screen for first 10 minutes of an incident)
  - Top row: requests/min (1m), error rate (1m), median token.latency ms (1m), p95 token.latency ms (1m)
  - Middle row: small heatmap of instance p95 latency by region x model (sparklines)
  - Bottom row: top 10 traces (by duration) with clickable trace id + small reproduction prompt (first 3 tokens + route)
  - Quick filters: tenant, model.version, region, time-window (last 5m/15m/1h)

2) KV warmness & eviction dashboard
  - Panel A: kv.prefix-hit-rate over time (5m rolling), tagged by model and instance pool
  - Panel B: eviction.rate per pool and eviction.reason (LRU|memory-pressure) stacked area
  - Panel C: cold-start incidents (count) + sample traces where the first token came from exec instead of kv, with trace link
  - Note: Show absolute numbers + normalized (per-1000 requests) to avoid misinterpreting activity spikes

3) Rollout readiness / lightweight canary view
  - For new model.version: compare baseline model vs canary across p50,p90,p99 token.latency, error.rate, and token-quality sampling (small sample of outputs for manual review)
  - Include a cost-velocity gauge (delta $/hour) and a guardrail blocker that flips state if error.rate > X or p99 latency > Y

Sampling & storage guidance (practical rules)
- Traces: adaptive sampling. Keep all traces flagged slow=true or error=true. For normal traffic, sample 2% of traces; increase sample to 10% for routes with >1% error rate.
- Event retention: keep high-cardinality debug traces for 14 days; aggregate traces/metrics beyond that to 90-day rollups. Store payload-free traces for 90 days for auditing purposes.
- Metric labels: avoid putting tenant-provided identifiers in high-cardinality labels (truncate or hash tenant.id where possible). Use tenant.tier tag for ops dashboards.

Investigation playbook (a compact flow for operators)
1) Confirm scope: check global request.count delta vs baseline; isolate region/model if spike is localized.
2) Open microtriage view, filter to 5m window. Look for divergence between p50 and p99 token latency.
3) If p99 is high but p50 stable: check batch.wait and queue-time spikes → suspect queuing/backpressure.
4) If both p50 and p95 increase: check exec.kernel memory/gpu.util and kernel.name → suspect model-level perf regression or kernel fallback.
5) If errors up: inspect top error.reason in error.rate; open representative traces (link) and look for auth.check or routing.lookup failures.
6) For KV warmness issues: open KV warmness dashboard, look for eviction.rate spikes or cluster rebalances.

Implementation notes / small heuristics I used during the rotation
- When adding p99 dashboards, include a secondary panel showing request volume — p99 jumps with tiny volumes are noise.
- Color mapping: use same palette for latency quantiles across dashboards to reduce operator context-switching (p50=blue, p90=amber, p99=red).
- Keep one reserved tiny panel for "recently-changed config" (last 24h) — often rollouts or opt-ins explain odd telemetry.

Unresolved questions / open items
- How do we expose token-quality sampling for production without leaking PII? Need a quick anonymization step in the sampling job. (Action: Priya to propose scrub rules, due 2026-02-05)
- Do we have a cheap way to correlate model.compile/kernel.fallback events in traces with rollout artifacts (git sha + build id)? If so we can automatically surface risky rollouts.
- KPI: should we set a soft p99 latency budget per model family rather than global? Ops feedback: yes, but needs mapping table.

References & quick links
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-6678 (obs dashboard patterns)
- Jira: JIRA-OBS-1423 (kv warmness follow-up work)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/obs-widgets/pull/89 (microdash layout prototype)

Notes to self
- Try an experimental panel that overlays p99 latency with sample token.source distribution (kv vs exec) — visible correlation is very convincing for SREs.
- Keep this doc small and portable; will copy the microdash wireframe into the rollout checklist page.

TODOs

- [ ] Priya to draft token-quality scrub rules (owner: Priya, ETA: 2026-02-05)
- [ ] Build microtriage dashboard prototype and run with oncall for two rotations (owner: Morgan, ETA: end of Feb)

---
End of notes.
